q: Does a bank's export credit to my company count as priority sector lending?
title: Export credit and priority sector lending
short: If your company is an MSME, yes: export credit to MSMEs counts under the MSME category, like any other MSME loan. For larger exporters, a domestic bank can count only the rise in export credit over the same date last year, up to 2% of its adjusted net bank credit, for borrowers with sanctioned limits up to ₹50 crore.
audience: Exporters, their finance heads and bank relationship managers

p: RBI's 2025 Directions define export credit as pre-shipment and post-shipment credit, as set out in its Credit Facilities Directions. Off-balance sheet items are excluded, so a guarantee or an unfunded letter of credit does not count.

Export credit to MSMEs and to agriculture is classified in those categories. Since all bank loans to MSMEs qualify as priority sector, a Udyam-registered exporter's packing credit or bill discounting counts in full under MSME, with no export-specific ceiling.

ul: Domestic banks, wholly owned subsidiaries of foreign banks, small finance banks and urban co-operative banks: only incremental export credit over the corresponding date of the previous year counts, up to 2% of adjusted net bank credit or the off-balance sheet equivalent, whichever is higher, and only for borrowers with a sanctioned limit up to ₹50 crore.
Foreign banks with 20 or more branches: incremental export credit up to the same 2% ceiling, with no per-borrower limit in the table.
Foreign banks with fewer than 20 branches: export credit can make up to 32% of adjusted net bank credit within their 40% priority sector target.
Regional rural banks and local area banks: this export credit rule does not apply.

p: Banks must lend 40% of adjusted net bank credit to the priority sector. A loan that counts towards that target is one a bank wants on its books, which helps when you negotiate limits. Classification alone does not fix your interest rate.

example.title: Example: a large exporter at a domestic bank (illustrative)
lines: Export credit outstanding on 30 June last year: ₹30 crore
Export credit outstanding on 30 June this year: ₹38 crore, sanctioned limit ₹45 crore
Eligible as priority sector: the ₹8 crore increase, within the bank's overall 2% ceiling
example.note: Figures are illustrative. A borrower with a sanctioned limit above ₹50 crore would not qualify at a domestic bank.

senseible: Senseible does not classify loans. For exporters it turns fuel and power bills into a dated emissions record that you can share with EU buyers who ask for one.
